extracted.intended_audience: Peer reviewers for the Journal of Social Science (JoSS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewing research manuscripts submitted to the Journal of Social Science (JoSS), describing what reviewers should evaluate in title, abstract, introduction, methods, results/discussion, conclusion, and overall presentation and writing. Intended to guide peer-review reports that assess clarity, rigor, novelty, and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this paper connect a cohesive argument? Are the ideas presented clearly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the manuscript presents a cohesive argument and whether ideas flow and are communicated clearly to the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing (clarity and concision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the title characterize the script? Is the writing concise and easy to follow?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate overall prose quality: concision, readability, and whether writing aids comprehension. Consider if the title appropriately characterizes the manuscript (see also Title guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and structural editing needs
rubrics_metrics.description: How much paper should be expanded? Deleted? Thick? Summarized? Combined?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate suggested structural edits and scope: which sections need expansion, deletion, condensation, summarization, or combination with other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the title succinct, omitting implied terms and, if possible, a statement of the main results or conclusions presented in the manuscript?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title should be succinct, avoid implied/implicit terms, and—if possible—state main results or conclusions. Abbreviations should be avoided in the title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the abstract consist of 1) research objectives; 2) method; 3) results or findings; and 4) conclusion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the abstract contains the four elements (objectives, method, results/findings, conclusion) so readers quickly grasp scope, approach, and key outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary / Introduction content
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe clearly and respectively: research background; state of the art; gap analysis; hypothesis/problem statement (optional); approach; research objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction (preliminary) should include: 1) Research background; 2) State of the art and relevant research to justify novelty; 3) Gap analysis / new statement; 4) Hypothesis or problem statement (optional); 5) Approach to solving problems; 6) Research objectives. Use these to judge whether the manuscript situates itself in the literature and justifies its contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method (replicability and detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods are clearly written so that other researchers can replicate the experiment or research with the same results; not only definitions but how to conduct the research; description of location, participants, instruments, and data analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether methods are sufficiently detailed for replication: include procedures, operational definitions, locations, participant descriptions, research instruments, and the data analysis approach. Avoid vague descriptions that prevent reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results and Discussion (data, interpretation, and implications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data should be processed (not raw) into tables/figures with descriptions; outcomes should relate to original questions; comparison with other research; scientific interpretation; explanation of implications; limitations; and suggestions for further research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate that: 1) Data are presented as processed tables/figures with explanatory captions/text (not raw data); 2) Outcomes address the questions/objectives in the Introduction; 3) Results are compared/contrasted with existing literature when relevant; 4) Author provides scientific interpretation for each finding; 5) Implications of the research are explained; 6) Limitations or methodological shortcomings are acknowledged; 7) Needs or directions for further research are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion (answers and format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consists of: 1) answering the research objectives; 2) implications or recommendations (optional); 3) written in paragraphs, not with bullets/numbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the conclusion explicitly answers the research objectives, may include implications/recommendations, and is presented as narrative paragraphs rather than lists or numbered points.
